name: effects-symbol-library-ticker
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.5) - Export As > SVG, Styling: Presentation Attributes, Object IDs: Layer Names
story: A news ticker strip: the designer built the channel bug once as an Illustrator symbol - plate, mark and the words "NOA 1" - and placed three instances of it, then set the rolling headline and the source credit as ordinary artboard text.
idioms: Generator comment: 'Adobe Illustrator 28.5.0, SVG Export Plug-In . SVG Version: 6.00 Build 0)'
Presentation Attributes styling: no <style> block anywhere, fill / font-family / font-size written on each element
<symbol  id="Channel_x20_bug" viewBox="0 0 120 40"> inside <defs>, with Illustrator's double space after the tag name
the symbol's own coordinate system (0 0 120 40), unrelated to the 1920x1080 artboard
_x20_ escape for the space in the symbol name, and #Channel_x20_bug in every reference
instances as <use xlink:href="#Channel_x20_bug"  width="120" height="40" x="0" y="0" transform="matrix(...)" overflow="visible"/> - xlink:href not href, and overflow="visible" on every one
two of the three instances scaled inside the matrix (matrix(0.6 0 0 0.6 100 992)) rather than by width/height
a <text> living inside the <symbol>, positioned by its own matrix transform in symbol space
font-size in px on the attribute (font-size="28px"), unitless letter-spacing="2"
text-anchor="end" on the right-hand credit, sharing one baseline with the headline
fill-opacity as its own attribute rather than opacity, on the ticker bar
tab indentation, one tab per nesting level
whyThisMatters: There are three "NOA 1"s on screen and only one text node behind them, so an importer that counts <text> elements anywhere in the document offers a field whose every keystroke rewrites all three bugs at once - and one that only skips it silently leaves the designer hunting for the missing layer; the file must give exactly two fields and one sentence saying why the third is not there.
